notes.reason: Liron is doing an impression, not giving a quote. He says "I also remember 2023, the CTO of Microsoft, Kevin Scott, got on a podcast, and he's like, 'Trust me, guys...'", and the words that follow are his own paraphrase of a remembered attitude. His point is about safety, not capability: he immediately adds "Smash cut to three years from now. They went outside of your data center and started rampaging." The note answers a different point. Its only source is a Microsoft-published interview dated 6 December 2022, not 2023, in which Scott is enthusiastic about what AI models can do and says nothing about whether models could escape or cause harm. Being bullish on capability is perfectly compatible with saying "there's nothing they can really do [to us]", so the quotes do not support the note's conclusion, and "No record supports this quote" is an unproven negative drawn from one PR interview. There may well be a real correction available here, since Scott was one of the few big-tech executives who signed the May 2023 statement on extinction risk from AI, but this note does not make that argument and instead reads as a gotcha on a spoken impression.

The note and the extracted claim do not match. The claim is about Aschenbrenner making roughly a 20X return, but the note never addresses that number and instead argues that he was not "relatively quiet". Liron's own sentence already says what the note tells him: "He's been relatively quiet in the last two years, but his fund has been under a lot of scrutiny." The whole segment that follows, titled "Leopold Aschenbrenner's Fund Crash", walks through the $45B peak, the margin call, the Citadel sale and the investor letter, so telling him the fund collapse was in the news at the time of the podcast corrects nothing. "Relatively quiet" plainly means quiet in public discourse, and the Situational Awareness essay was June 2024, which is just over two years before this 31 July 2026 episode, so even read literally he is not wrong. The note's facts are true but they are aimed at a statement the author does not make.

The note is itself wrong about the April incident. Anthropic's own writeup, which this episode links to, says "The earliest incidents date to April" and describes three incidents in which Claude reached real systems outside Anthropic: exploiting a real company's infrastructure and reading several hundred rows of production data, publishing a malicious PyPI package that was downloaded and run on 15 real systems, and scanning roughly 9,000 targets. So "not hacking external targets" is false for the April incident. The note also treats the July and August 2026 disclosures as "separate tests months later", but July is when Anthropic ran its review and went public, not when the behaviour happened. The 0.01% figure the note leans on comes from a third-party developer blog describing a different thing, the reward hacking seen during Mythos's reinforcement learning, so the note swaps in another event. There is a small real error in the passage, since the April incident was Claude Opus 4.7 rather than Mythos 5 and it happened in an evaluation rather than in training, but Liron flags his own uncertainty ("I'm not even clear on what they hacked... I need to look into this more") and the note does not make that correction.
